fed.probabilities_note: Market-implied Fed path, read from the curve instead of the licensed CME futures feed: the gap between the 1-year Treasury and the current target midpoint. Positive = easing priced, negative = tightening priced. A real signal, not an option-implied probability.
fed.caveat: The Fed does not set mortgage rates. It moves the front end; mortgage rates follow the 10Y and the MBS spread.

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 4.98%, +10 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.18%, -6 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 234 bp, normal at the 66th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.34 points of the 7.18% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
10-Year Treasury +10 bp, bigger than 95% of moves on record. Expect rate sheets to follow.
Core CPI +0.30% (2026-10 reference month), the newest inflation read the market has.

why.headline: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 4.98% (+10 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.31%.
why.summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.98%, +10 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -6 bp. That breaks down exactly: -14 bp from Treasuries and +8 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 234 bp, which is normal and sits at the 66th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 26 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.

contributions.chain: Payrolls → ↓ Recession risk → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Recession fear is the classic bid for duration. Yields fall.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

brief.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
brief.body: Mortgage rates: 7.18% published 2026-11-05, modeled 7.31% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.98% (+10 bp). MBS: -14.00 ticks. Rate bias: Worsening. The mortgage spread is 234 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Consumer Price Index on 11-12, Core CPI on 11-12. Biggest risk: Consumer Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: protect anything closing inside 30 days and expect reprice risk intraday
